minutes.headline: Capital Planning heard the school department's 10-year plan, led by Turkey Hill and the turf field; no spending votes taken.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a resident's stormwater complaint, then the school department's building-by-building capital requests, mainly turf field drainage, Turkey Hill studies and repairs, primary school playground and driveway, and vehicles. Members debated technology as capital versus operating, MSBA funding and financing mechanics. The only vote was approving the October 23rd minutes; the group planned a November 29th meeting and a ranking process.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee heard the school department's 10-year capital requests, led by Turkey Hill and the turf field complex; no spending votes were taken.
The turf field plan has a funded first-phase assessment and a second phase requesting more money for detailed engineering.

Members questioned whether classroom technology belongs in capital rather than the operating budget, and asked that Turkey Hill costs listed as the town's share after state reimbursement also show the total.
The only vote was approval of the October 23rd minutes; the committee tentatively set November 29th to meet again.
The committee plans about three meetings to finalize, ending in an individual ranking from a spreadsheet and then a final ranking.

why_it_matters: The capital plan decides which school building and field projects compete for town borrowing and funds, and the ranking process begun here shapes what residents may later be asked to vote on.
Several costs are shown only as the town's share after state building-authority reimbursement, so a resident cannot yet see the full price of the Turkey Hill work.
watch_next: Tentative November 29th meeting, with a facilities presentation expected.
The individual ranking spreadsheet from the town manager, and the corrected school slides to be posted.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on most of the shared budget figures (turf phases 1 and 2, Turkey Hill study, windows, technology and HVAC, playground design), on the November 29 meeting, and on who attended, apart from two caption misspellings. The one real conflict is the Turkey Hill roof, which ours hears as about $1.25 million and the official minutes print as $625,000. Our figures for grass-field maintenance, mini splits, the $24 million out-year total and the $75,000 stormwater item are not in the official minutes, and that record also lists many items (turf phases 3 and 4, fire suppression, Primary School, vehicles) that we did not capture.
